children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

apprenticeship_location.description: The country where the child has started an apprenticeship, where relevant.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children that you're responsible for?** If yes, how many children do you have, and what are their ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have a child I'm responsible for. His name is Alex and he's 19 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since Alex is 19 years old, I need to ask you an important question:

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?**

(Child Benefit can continue for children aged 16-19 if they remain in approved education or training)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in approved education at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. I have one more important question:

**Has Alex recently left education or training, and if so, has he registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services?**

(You can still get Child Benefit for up to 20 weeks after a 16 or 17 year old leaves education if they register with these services, but this only applies to those aged 16-17)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't registered with any careers service or the armed forces. He's 19, so I don't think that applies to him anyway.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. Let me also confirm a few more details to complete my assessment:

**Do you live in the UK, and does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK. But no, Alex doesn't live with me - he lives elsewhere.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. This is an important detail. 

**Are you making financial contributions towards Alex's upkeep?** For example, are you paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit (or the equivalent in kind) towards looking after him - such as for food, clothes, pocket money, or contributing to his accommodation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do contribute towards his upkeep. I help with things like clothes and other expenses - I give about £30 a week.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for providing all that information. Let me assess Alex's eligibility for Child Benefit based on what you've told me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Assessment Complete

Based on the information you've provided, **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

- Alex is 19 years old
- Child Benefit is normally available for children under 16, **or** for young people aged 16-19 if they remain in approved education or training
- Since Alex is not currently in approved education or training, he does not meet the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit

While you do contribute financially towards Alex's upkeep, the fundamental requirement is that children aged 16-19 must be in approved education or training to qualify. Unfortunately, Alex doesn't meet this requirement.

If Alex's circumstances change in the future (for example, if he enters approved education or training), you may wish to reconsider applying at that time.
